newsitem.title: USA: ARMSTRONG SEEKS INDEPENDENT DIRECTORS FOR DOMCO.
newsitem.headline: ARMSTRONG SEEKS INDEPENDENT DIRECTORS FOR DOMCO.

text.p: Armstrong World Industries Inc said Monday it amended a claim it brought against the board of Domco Inc asking an Ontario court to select independent directors to replace the Canadian flooring manufacturer's board.
It said it wanted independent directors to make a fresh consideration of the Domco board's decision not to issue new shares that Armstrong could subscribe to.
In addition to shares it may buy in its hostile C$23 a share bid, the subscription, if allowed, would give flooring giant Armstrong 51 percent of Domco's shares on a fully diluted basis.

In a statement, Armstrong said it hopes the Ontario court will uphold its view that the current Domco board "has breached duties that it owes by its failure to obtain value" for all Domco shareholders. Domco rejected the Armstrong bid last week.

French concern Sommer Allibert, which holds 69.2 percent of Domco's shares or 57.1 percent on a fully diluted basis, has said it would not sell its Domco shares to Armstrong. In the spring, Sommer entered into a deal to combine its flooring business with that of Germany's Tarkett AG .

In its statement, Armstrong's chief financial officer, Frank Riddick III, said that the Domco board, "has insulted the intelligence of its shareholders by claiming that Domco is not in play and that therefore they will take no action to issue shares to Armstrong to enable the 51 percent minimum condition to become a reality -- clearly an act they have the power to do."
A spokeswoman for Domco was not immediately available to comment.
